title: Connexions de Gauss-Manin et équations de Picard-Fuchs. Opération de Cartier : copies de tapuscrit annoté (s.d.), tiré à part (1981), notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context. The neighbouring pages give the setting. X is over S in characteristic p, with relative Frobenius X → X^{(p/S)} and Λ = image of O_{X^{(p)}} in O_X, so that X_0^{(p)} = (X^{(p/S)}, Λ). A connection on O_X (or on a line bundle) is written ∇ = ∇_0 + ω, where ω is a relative 1-form. The proposition being proved has two parts:
(1) ∇ is integrable iff dω = 0.
(2) ∇ is compatible with p-th powers (p-curvature zero) iff C̃ω = ω̃.
Here C̃ is the relative Cartier operator and ω̃ is the p-th-power image of ω in Ω^1_{X^{(p)}/S} ⊗ Λ.

This page finishes the local computation for (2).
- Choose a p-basis (x_i) with D_i = ∂/∂x_i, so D_i^p = 0 and [D_i, D_j] = 0.
- Write ω = Σ c_i dx_i, so the operator for D_i is Δ_i = Δ_i^0 + c_i.
- Jacobson's formula (cited from Sém. Chevalley 58/59, exp. 6) gives (Δ_i^0 + c_i)^p = Δ_i^{0p} + c_i^p + D_i^{p-1}(c_i), with Δ_i^{0p} = 0 by hypothesis.
- So p-curvature zero is equivalent to (*) c_i^p + D_i^{p-1} c_i = 0 for all i.

Next, d ω = 0 reads (**) D_i c_j = D_j c_i. For closed ω, Cartier's explicit formula (loc. cit. p. 05, prop. 3) gives (***) C̃ω = Σ_i −D_i^{p-1}(c_i) (dx̃_i ⊗ 1_Λ). The coefficient −D_i^{p-1}c_i lies in Λ, since it equals ⟨D_i, Cω⟩·1_Λ. Meanwhile ω̃ = Σ c_i^p (dx̃_i ⊗ 1_Λ). Hence ω̃ − C̃ω = Σ (c_i^p + D_i^{p-1} c_i)(dx̃_i ⊗ 1_Λ), which vanishes iff (*) holds.

The page then invokes Cartier/Frobenius descent: an integrable connection with zero p-curvature on a quasi-coherent module is the same as descent data to (X^{(p)}, Λ). The next page uses this to deduce a relative form of Cartier's theorem: ω is locally df/f iff dω = 0 and C̃ω = ω̃. Equivalently, the image of dlog: O_X^* → Ω^1_{X/S} is that subsheaf, with kernel Λ^*.

In short, this is the rank-one case of 'p-curvature = Frobenius pullback of (ω − Cω)', worked out over an arbitrary base S.
errors: No mathematical error. The sign in (***) is correct: in one variable C(x^{p-1}dx) = dx, and D^{p-1}(x^{p-1}) = (p-1)! = -1.

Minor gap: checking Θ_{D_i}^p = 0 only on the basis D_i suffices only because, given integrability (dω = 0), the p-curvature is p-linear and additive in the derivation. The previous page asserts this sufficiency via a presentation of the algebra of differential operators but does not fully argue it.
Jacobson's formula as written uses D_i^{p-1}c_i for ad(Δ_i)^{p-1}(c_i). This is legitimate because Δ_i^0 acts on functions as the derivation D_i, so the commutator just differentiates c_i.

ideas.what: Jacobson's formula (D+c)^p = D^p + c^p + D^{p-1}(c), applied to p-curvature of a rank-one connection
ideas.usually_credited_to: N. Jacobson; P. Cartier (Sém. Chevalley 1958/59); N. Katz (1970)
ideas.where_published: Katz, 'Nilpotent connections and the monodromy theorem', Publ. IHES 39 (1970)

ideas.what: Explicit formula for the Cartier operator on closed 1-forms: Cω = Σ (−D_i^{p-1}c_i)^{1/p} dx_i, in relative form
p-curvature of ∇_0 + ω vanishes iff C̃ω = ω̃; obstruction ω̃ − C̃ω as a section of Ω^1 (End(E)-valued in general)
ideas.modern_name: p-curvature of rank-one connections, ψ(d+ω) = F*(ω) − F*C(ω)

ideas.what: Integrable connection with zero p-curvature is equivalent to descent along Frobenius
Relative Cartier theorem: locally logarithmic 1-forms are exactly those with dω = 0 and C̃ω = ω̃, over an arbitrary base S, with kernel Λ^*
ideas.modern_name: Cartier's theorem on logarithmic differentials (relative version)

deep.surprise_reason: This is a careful but standard verification, essentially Katz 1970 §7 together with Cartier's theorem, done relatively over a possibly non-reduced base using Λ instead of O^p. The only mildly distinctive points are: working with Λ (the image of O_{X^{(p)}}) rather than assuming S reduced, and the marginal suggestion on the previous page to define the obstruction (i.e. p-curvature) for higher rank. Both are known.
transcription_corrections: The displayed formula reads (Δ_i + c_i)^p = Δ_i^p + c_i^p + D_i^{p-1} c_i, with '‖ 0 par hyp' under Δ_i^p. It is not (D_i + c_i)^p = D_i^p + ...; the operators are Δ_i (Δ_i^0), not D_i.
In the line 'Or écrivons que ... Cω = ω̃', the inserted 'dω=0' sits above, and C carries a tilde (C̃ω = ω̃).
Under the brace in (***), the annotation reads 'est dans Λ car égal à ⟨D_i, Cω⟩1_Λ'.
The left-margin note reads 'indiquer dans la formulation des §3.-§4' and refers to the bracketed remark '[c'est-à-dire ... la formule de transposition ... de loc. cit. p. 05 (prop. 3)]'.
